metaData.originalTitle: OpenSandbox 再进化：Credential Vault 让真实密钥不再进入沙箱
metaData.title: OpenSandbox Evolved: Credential Vault Keeps Real Secrets Out of the Sandbox
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: OpenSandbox introduces the Credential Vault feature, which injects credentials outside the sandbox via an egress proxy, eliminating the need for AI Agent sandboxes to store real secrets.
metaData.summary: The article analyzes the security risks of using secrets directly within AI Agent sandboxes, such as Prompt Injection, malicious dependencies, and log leaks. It then introduces OpenSandbox's new Credential Vault solution: real credentials are stored outside the sandbox, and an egress sidecar injects authentication information into outbound requests based on rules; only fake values are used inside the sandbox, ensuring that secrets never enter environment variables, command lines, file systems, or logs. The article uses typical scenarios like Claude Code calling model APIs, cloning private Git repositories, and accessing internal APIs to illustrate how it works, and recommends pairing it with a default-deny egress network policy to achieve finer-grained security boundaries. It also notes that it currently does not support coexistence with transparent service mesh sidecars. Finally, it concludes that this feature advances sandbox isolation from the process/file/network layer to the credential isolation layer, serving as a crucial complement to the productionization of AI Agents.

mainPoints.point: Directly exposing secrets inside the sandbox amplifies risks like Prompt Injection, malicious dependencies, and log leaks.
mainPoints.explanation: AI Agent execution paths are long and unpredictable; once secrets enter sandbox environment variables, command lines, or configuration files, a loss of control at any point in the toolchain can lead to secret leakage.

mainPoints.point: Credential Vault injects authentication information into outbound requests via an egress sidecar, keeping only fake values inside the sandbox.
mainPoints.explanation: The host SDK writes real credentials and binding rules into the sidecar, while the sandbox process only holds fake API Keys; when a matching outbound request passes through, the sidecar automatically injects the real auth header, ensuring secrets never enter the sandbox.

mainPoints.point: This solution applies to various developer tool scenarios, such as model APIs, Git clones, and internal APIs.
mainPoints.explanation: Whether it is HTTP Basic Auth, Header Token, or complex path matching, Credential Vault can achieve precise authorization through binding rules.

mainPoints.point: It is recommended to pair with a default-deny egress network policy to achieve multi-dimensional binding of credentials to services, paths, and methods.
mainPoints.explanation: Only allow the service hosts that tools truly need, and then use the Vault to restrict credentials to a narrower request scope, enhancing the precision of security boundaries.

mainPoints.point: Currently, it does not support coexistence with transparent service mesh sidecars like Istio/Envoy.
mainPoints.explanation: Two layers of sidecars will conflict within the same network namespace, so platforms must pay attention to the compatibility of deployment environments.

keyQuotes: Real secrets should stay outside the sandbox, injected by the platform based on rules over a controlled egress path.
The sandbox handles execution, the Vault handles authorization, and the egress policy handles the boundary.
Credential Vault is not about making it more convenient for the sandbox to store secrets, but about making it so the sandbox no longer needs to store real secrets.

relatedArticles.title: AI Doesn't Lack Intelligence, It Lacks Discipline: A Harness Engineering Practice
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically reviews the author's complete journey in Harness engineering practice, evolving AI Coding from 'stacking prompt constraints' to a 'structured framework' through layered constraints, externalized state, and deterministic evaluation.

relatedArticles.title: Standards and Paths for AI-Friendly Backend Architecture: System Refactoring for the Unattended Development Era
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically proposes standards and transformation paths for making backend architectures 'AI-Friendly,' with the core idea being to convert system knowledge from human brain assets into machine-readable structured assets, enabling AI Agents to safely and efficiently participate in development, troubleshooting, and operations within limited contexts.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Rethinking Development Infrastructure: When Agents Become First-Class Citizens
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes a unified framework of 'intent-driven + code precipitation', arguing that agents do not change the fundamental structure of software evolution but compress the 'intent → code' cycle from months/weeks to minutes, and thus deduces that development infrastructure must shift from People-Oriented to Agent-Oriented design principles.

relatedArticles.title: From Language Emergence to Collaborative Emergence: How to Enable AI to Produce High-Quality Decisions
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This paper introduces the Agent Room concept, which enables a leap from process automation to collaborative emergence by placing multiple AI agents in a shared context field, thereby producing higher-quality collective decisions.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Redefining Skill Development: A Step-by-Step Guide & One-Stop Development Assistant Launch
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces the concept of AI Agent Skill, including its directory structure, writing standards, release process, and cross-platform challenges. It also launches a one-stop Skill development assistant, skill-dev-aio, designed to free developers from tedious tool learning and allow them to focus on experience and judgment.

relatedArticles.title: The AI Native Era: Where Is R&D Organization Headed?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the paradigm shift of R&D organizations in the AI Native era, proposing that organizational structures will evolve from human-centric Org Charts to Execution Graphs that include both humans and AI Agents, and systematically analyzes core issues such as new bottlenecks, management collapse, and the governance of three types of work.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.
